<p class="hero-name">Glory Kellogg</p>

I am an Applied Mathematics Honors student at the Illinois Institute of Technology pursuing a minor in Computer Science.

I'm drawn to the hidden patterns of the natural world and to the math that helps bring them into focus.
Lately, I’ve been wondering how butterfly wings form patterns and why some networks become unequal.

I've started keeping a [library](library.qmd) of books and papers with notes on the ideas that have shaped my thinking. You can also read my [curriculum vitae](curriculum-vitae.qmd) or [send me an email](mailto:gloryekellogg@gmail.com).

## Current Research

<div class="project-grid">
<a class="project-card" href="butterfly-wings.html">
  <h3>Butterfly Wing Pattern Formation</h3>
  <p>
    Mathematical and computational models of butterfly wing development,
    including image processing, graph representations, and reaction–diffusion systems.
  </p>
</a>
<a class="project-card" href="collaboration-networks.html">
  <h3>Collaboration Networks</h3>
  <p>
    An agent-based model examining how nonlinear preferential attachment
    shapes network growth, inequality, and concentration.
  </p>
</a></div>
